observations.classification: Conditional financial-presentation/reconciliation risk; not confirmed defect
observations.evidence: ComposeShiftCloseSlipAsync preserves saved Shift ExpectedCash/ActualCash/CashDifference where present but recomputes breakdown components and paid-from-drawer expense categories from current rows through ShiftReconciliation. Reprint calls the current-data calculation path. Printing does not mutate financial ledgers.
observations.counterevidence: Close handler uses the same reconciliation helper; stored headline close figures are preserved. This can be intended current-state explanatory detail. Post-close mutation/revision policy and immutability of contributing rows were not reviewed/established.
observations.impact: If relevant source rows can change after close, visible breakdown can stop summing to the frozen headline. No close/payment/cash/expense mutation is evidenced.
observations.owner_question: Must reprinted close slips reproduce the exact close-time breakdown, or can explanatory components reflect current row state?
observations.proposed_resolution: If historical reproduction is required, persist immutable close-time components or version/source-row revision identifiers. If current recomputation is intended, label it and retain frozen headline distinction.
tests: Close then mutate/correct a contributing order/refund/expense/movement in an approved isolated test DB; compare original vs reprinted breakdown and frozen headline.
Reopen/revise only through authorized flow, then verify old and new close revisions render the intended snapshot.
Verify print/reprint never changes financial journal or shift close values.
observations.acceptance: Reprint semantics are documented and tests prove each close revision is stable or explicitly current/recomputed; print operations remain ledger-nonmutating.

observations.classification: Requirements-dependent presentation scope concern; no accounting impact established
observations.evidence: PrintJobQueryService.LoadCloseWarningsAsync filters pending electronic/unpaid orders by shift but selects all open DriverCustodies by status without delivery ShiftId join. DeliveryRules.UnsettledCustodyForShift is shift-filtered; its test excludes cross-shift custody. The close handler/comment permits global handover context and same-shift integration test verifies warning inclusion only.
observations.counterevidence: Unsettled custody may intentionally be restaurant-wide/business-day context; owner requirement is absent. The warning does not affect expected cash, close eligibility or treasury movements.
observations.owner_question: Should the shift handover warning show only custody tied to that shift, or all outstanding driver custody across the restaurant/business day?
observations.proposed_resolution: If shift-scoped, join open custody through delivery ShiftId. If intentionally global, label the warning as global/business-day wide. Do not alter global business-day close blockers without separate evidence.
tests: Create two shifts with open delivery custody on only one shift; close the other and verify warning wording/scope.
Assert no financial movements or close amount changes from warning aggregation.
observations.acceptance: Owner-defined scope is explicit in labels and cross-shift test; ledger and close arithmetic are unchanged.
